parsed.title: Fake Tax-Themed Phishing Campaign Delivers Malware
parsed.summary: A fake Indian Income Tax Department campaign uses ten disposable .shop domains to distribute malware through a fabricated Section 143(3) Notice of Assessment. Victims are lured into downloading a VHDX disk image disguised as an offline ITR-1 to ITR-4 utility, which when mounted reveals a loader executable and a DLL payload. The loader injects code into RuntimeBroker.exe and attempts a TCP/443 connection to a suspected C2 endpoint, though no C2 communication was established. The malware is assessed to have RAT-like capabilities, including persistence, system discovery, and remote command execution. The campaign is unattributed, and defenders should restrict mounting of VHDX files and monitor execution chains from mounted disk images.
